answer: In an attestation graph, trust is propagated by bounded random walks from independently anchored users. A sybil cluster cannot gain voting weight merely by adding internal edges: its sparse external cut limits the probability that those walks enter it. When weight is tied to reachable anchor mass and capped using conductance or min-cut bounds, low-conductance clusters receive only the support justified by genuine cross-cut attestations; an inlet, beacon, or oasis label cannot change that bound.
